title: Adaptive mesh refinement in a sloshing tank
author: Mohammadreza Khani, PhD
scope: Independent two-dimensional method demonstration with assumed tank geometry and operating conditions.

solver.name: Basilisk
solver.interface: native PLIC segments plus pure-phase face jumps

AMR.criterion: custom geometric interface distance; not a wavelet error estimator
AMR.whole_cell_allowance: subtract half the cell diagonal from centre-to-interface distance; floor at zero
AMR.face_flux_repair_potential: auxiliary numerical potential, separate from physical pressure

video.amber: refined descendants compared with preceding saved native grid
video.purple: coarsened parents fully tiled by preceding finer native leaves
video.mesh_change_sampling: changes between saved grids, not individual AMR event counts

numerical_status.termination: longer calculation failed its physical pressure-projection guard after the retained prefix

model_assumptions.geometry: assumed analytic section represented by a fixed Cartesian full-cell wall

workflow: AI assists workflow scripting, post-processing and technical communication; Basilisk performs the numerical flow calculation.
interpretation: Computed interface fragmentation is qualitative. Numerical/output checks do not establish experimentally validated breakup, three-dimensional droplet prediction or a mesh-converged result.
